name: deepcoro-ivus-oct
instructions: Watch the whole cine. Q1: is an intravascular imaging catheter inside a coronary artery? OCT = thin catheter with a short radiopaque lens marker, usually imaged during a continuous contrast flush that clears the vessel while the marker pulls back. IVUS = thicker catheter with a visible transducer segment, usually filmed under plain fluoroscopy (no contrast) during pullback. A guidewire, balloon or stent delivery system alone is 'Other device only'. Q2-Q4 only if Q1 is OCT, IVUS or uncertain: vessel where the imaging catheter sits, and whether the pullback/flush is visible. Record coronary_system for imaging catheters and other devices (wire/balloon/stent). Left coronary may include LAD and LCX together; do not infer left-main traversal. Original detailed vessel answers are retained.
